To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the replication of oncolytic MYXV in human cancer cells is regulated positively and negatively through the activity of host RNA helicase proteins.
five DEAD-box RNA helices (DDX3, DDX5/6, DDX52, DHX9 and DHX37) are anti-viral, and three (DDX3/5, DHX29, DHx35) are pro-viral or required for permissive cancer cells.

(1) MYXV tropisms in human cancer cells are regulated by multiple host RNA helicase proteins, which are required for viral replication or host metabolic functions, and (2) the RNA helicase DDX52 is a novel host restriction factor for MYXV replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how host DEAD-box RNA-helicases regulate MYXV replication in human cancer cells and how the virus can be used for the treatment of human cancers.

the identification of host DEAD-box proteins that regulate MYXV replication in permissive and nonpermissive human cancer cells, and their potential role as therapeutic targets for the development of oncolytic viropharmaceuticals for the treatment of cancer.
the identification of cellular factors relevant for the replication of MYXVM, and the subsequent development of a small molecule inhibitor to target the identified cellular factor(s).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MYXV replication is dramatically regulated by host DEAD-box RNA Helicases.
DEAD-box RNA helices are important for MYXV replication in human cancer cells and likely all poxyviruses.
MYXV replication is dramatically regulated by multiple host DEAD box RNA helicases, both positively and negatively, in a cell type-dependent manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MYXV infection of cancer cells is regulated by host DEAD-box RNA Helicases, and that these host RNA helicase factors may be exploited as novel therapeutic targets to enhance MYXV replication for oncolytic virotreatments.
MYXV is permissive for the vast majority of human cancer cell lines, but a minority is nonpermissive because of the virus aborts its replication cycle before its completion.
MYXV is highly permissive for human cancer cells because of a lack of antiviral signaling pathways and the virus exploits cellular RNA helicase activities to facilitate its replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DEAD-box RNA helices are important regulators of poxvirus replication in human cancer cells and thus are potential targets for the development of novel oncolytic virotreatments.
MYXV tropisms are not only determined by the viral gene expression and replication programs but also by the cellular RNA helicase machinery.
DEAD-box RNA helicas are critical host factors for MYXV replication in human cancer cells.
